newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico cold snap kills baby.
newsitem.headline: Mexico cold snap kills baby.

text.p: A cold snap that sent temperatures plummeting to 19 degrees (-7 Celsius) in northern Mexico claimed the life of a baby on Monday and caused a spate of traffic accidents, officials said.
The death lifted the toll from cold winter weather in Nuevo Leon state to 17 since Nov. 15. Snow fell in parts of Nuevo Leon overnight on Sunday, leaving roads slick and icy.
Sub-freezing temperatures are rare in Mexico, as is snow below the highest mountaintops.

"Early this morning a baby died, and with that the total this winter, from Nov. 15, has risen to 17 people killed directly or indirectly from the cold," Oswaldo Flores Gomez, chief of the State Civil Protection Council, told Reuters.
Of the total, seven babies and two adults have died from lung problems related to the cold and eight people have died from leaking gas heaters, Flores said.

The wave of cold Arctic air pushing down through North America has hit northern Mexico particularly hard in recent days, bringing freezing temperatures to the states of Chihuahua, Sonora and Baja California as well.
